Scope

The whole Etana epic as eBL edits it (L/1/9), all six chapters, 585 lines:

Key eBL chapter Lines Manuscripts (eBL sigla) Content
OBM Old Babylonian, Morgan 54 (1–16, a+1–a+13, b+1–b+16, c+1–c+9) BabaOB1 (MLC 1363, the "Morgan tablet"; Scheil's copy RT 23) the gods without a king; kingship comes down from heaven; Etana takes a wife?; the serpent's revenge; the eagle in the pit; Etana frees him: "open my eyes to what is hidden"
OBS Old Babylonian, Susa 48 (1–24, a+1–a+24) the Susa tablet the oath's curses; both give birth under the poplar; the shared hunt; the eagle's plot; the fledgling; the serpent's lament
MA Middle Assyrian, Aššur 160 (a+1 … i+18) AššMA1–2 (at least two tablets) the oath, the friendship, the hunt, the plot, the ambush; Etana's dream; the rescue; the dreams; the flight
I Standard Babylonian I 40 (1–29, a+1–a+11) Nineveh the city planned, no king, Ištar seeks a shepherd; Etana's wife's dream
II Standard Babylonian II 152 Nineveh the shrine of Adad and the poplar; the oath; the plot; Šamaš's ambush; the pit; Etana's prayer; the eagle found
III Standard Babylonian III 131 (1–56, a+1–a+23, b+1–b+45, c+1–c+7) Nineveh the speech of birds; the first flight (Etana gives up); return; the dreams; the second flight to the gates of the gods

Base text: ../../sources/eBL/Etana-OB-Morgan/ … Etana-SB-III/ (reading-edition.md: normalization N, Foster's
translation T, lemmas L, notes, parallels, ATF; glossary.md; generated by tools/ebl_fetch.py on 2026-10-21; git-
ignored, restorable with tools/sources_sync.py). Edition: Z. J. Földi (ed.), rev. A. Hätinen, E. Jiménez,
G. Rozzi (eBL 2026, with J. Novotny's digital edition); translation B. R. Foster. The end of the epic is lost.

Files

  • annotated-OBM.rtl.md, annotated-OBS.rtl.md, annotated-MA.rtl.md, annotated-I.rtl.md, annotated-II.rtl.md,
    annotated-III.rtl.md: one per eBL chapter; entries ### <KEY>.<eBL label> (### II.45, ### MA.c+3), in eBL's
    order. The first line of each file after the title is <!-- כותרת־נוסח: … --> (the version heading of the clean
    translation).
  • translation--intro.rtl.md (the coordinator), translation.rtl.md (generated: python3 -I ../kings_tools.py build ET;
    it prints the eBL label without the chapter key, under the version heading).
  • Tools: python3 -I ../kings_tools.py verify ET [--strict], data ET <from> <to> <out> (the eBL block of each line +
    its related lines in all six versions with the Hebrew already given), pars ET <from> <to>, lines ET <from>-<to>,
    grep all '<regex>' (all corpora, Sumerian and Akkadian).

Line numbering

eBL's labels (George-style: a+1 = the first preserved line after a gap of unknown length). The literature's older
numbering (Kinnier Wilson 1985; Foster; Dalley; Haul 2000) differs (e.g. SB II = Kinnier Wilson's "Tablet II"); eBL's
Parallels: field gives the correspondences between the versions. No concordance to older numbering is made here.

Open decisions (the coordinator's summary, 2026-10-22)

Each part's numbered list is in its section below; the minor ones were decided there (the user's rule) and merged into
../renderings.md §10.6. Nothing major is left for the user. Left for the next cross-corpus harmonization (they
touch other corpora, which other Round 3 sessions were editing; listed in ../../STATUS.md §6):

  1. šarāku הֶעֱנִיק (= Sum. rig₇, EA) vs Gilgameš qiāšu הֶעֱנִיק (two verbs, one Hebrew).
  2. Enki and the World Order's boat אקו־האפסו (taraḫ) vs taraḫ = turāḫu = יָעֵל (EA, Agade, Etana) and armu =
    אַקּוֹ (Etana): proposal יעל־האפסו.
  3. ḫaṭṭu שרביט (here, EA) vs שבט (Enūma eliš IV 29, LH): proposal שרביט for ḫaṭṭu everywhere, שבט for
    šabbiṭu only.
  4. parakku כֵּס (here, EA barag) vs דוכן (Enūma eliš); Sum. aga עטרת (EWO 264) vs agû כתר (Gilgameš). Settled 2026-10-23 (../../harmonization--2026-10-23.md row 5): parakku = דּוּכָן (I.15, I.23, II.3, II.4, OBM.9).
  5. palgu תעלה (here) vs the cognate פֶּלֶג (Enūma eliš): proposal פֶּלֶג everywhere. Settled 2026-10-23 (../../harmonization--2026-10-23.md row 7): פֶּלֶג (MA.i+10 [כ]מי פלג).
  6. buginnu שוקת (here; = Sum. buniĝ, Gudea) vs Gilgameš mašqû שוקת: proposal mašqû מַשְׁקֶה.
  7. Smaller splits recorded by the parts: šērtu עֹנֶשׁ (Atra-ḫasīs, here) vs אַשְׁמָה (Gilgameš, Ludlul); ērišu
    חתן vs Gilgameš ḫāmiru; nāʾeru שואג vs צורח; ṣapāru / raʾzu משובץ; ḫiāṭu בחן vs barû בוחן;
    ina ūmīšu ביום ההוא vs בעת ההיא; galātu התפלץ vs Sum. ḫuluḫ נבהל; qarānu ערם beside Sum. dub.

Part ET1 – before the king (OB Morgan 1–a+13; SB I 1–a+11), 2026-10-22

Round 3, run 2 (../renderings.md §10.5). Translator: sub-agent ET1. Files: annotated-OBM.rtl.md (header for the
whole tablet + 1–16, a+1–a+13; ET3 adds one paragraph on its lines and b+1–c+9), annotated-I.rtl.md (the whole
tablet: header + 1–29, a+1–a+11). 69 entries. Not committed.

Progress and passes

  • Order of work: OB Morgan first (it fixes the Hebrew of the prologue), then SB I, copying the OB Hebrew wherever
    the Akkadian is the same (OBM 1–10 ≈ I 8–17; OBM a+2 ≈ I a+2) and varying only where it varies; both entries of each
    pair say what the other version has.
  • Data: kings_tools.py data ET for both ranges; eBL dictionary per word (ṣapāru, saḫāru, ištēniš, dapnu, šibirru,
    meānu, mitluku, šiāti); every transliteration precedent searched in the annotated files of all corpora (a scratch
    helper that greps the backticked lines and prints the Hebrew) and every new Hebrew word with kings_tools.py grep all.
    Every Bible verse printed with check_bible_quotes.py --show before quoting.
  • Pass (a) fidelity: every > line against N and the ATF. Fixed: I.4 האל[ים? (the ATF has DINGIR#-[MEŠ?: the
    word is there, only the plural sign is broken; eBL's N brackets the whole word); I.1 note that āla īṣirū is broken
    on NinNA1 but preserved in the incipit quotations (hence no brackets); I.a+3 the tablet's šu-ut-tu (nom.) against
    N's šutta; OBM.13 ⟨ל⟩ for the scribe's omitted <a-na>; I.15 the scribe's superfluous kibrāti (dittography from
    I.10) left untranslated, with a note.
  • Pass (b) consistency: the OB/SB pairs compared line by line (identical Hebrew where identical Akkadian:
    הָאֲנוּנָּכִּי … גוזרי, בוני קצות (הארץ), לאנשים, חג, גזרו, שָׂמוּ, מלך, ושרביט – ספיר לא משובץ,
    לא בנויים – יחדיו – הַכֵּסִים, נעל-; I.1 = I.3, I.2 = I.4, I.19 ~ I.21, I.20 = I.22); renderings §10.4 checked
    (מצנפת, עטרה, שרביט, כֵּס, רועה, המלכות – מן השמים ירדה, לְבֵנָה, אִט); every new word grepped in all
    corpora (collisions listed under open decisions 2–8).
  • Pass (c) Hebrew: read aloud; vocalized what would be misread: יָצְרוּ (not "besieged"), לְבֵנָתָהּ, הַכֵּסִים
    (not "pockets"), שָׂמוּ / שׂוּמִים / שָׂמֵי, בָּהּ, נִמְלָךְ, רוֹעָן, בַּנָּאָן, אֵלֵי, אֶל?, מוֹתָם, אִטּוֹ,
    קַח, כּוֹנְנוּ, הֶרְ[אַנִי; names (אֵתָנָה, אִשְׁתַּר, אָנוּ) at every occurrence in the > lines and headings.
  • Checks: python3 -I kings_tools.py verify ET – 248 entries, OK (no problem; only the coverage note for the parts
    not yet drafted). python3 -I ../tools/check_bible_quotes.py annotated-OBM.rtl.md annotated-I.rtl.md (and this file) –
    0 problems.

Deviations from renderings §10 and the guidelines (decided at the first occurrence, with the reason)

  1. eṣēru = יָצַר, written יָצְרוּ (vocalized), not the צָר of guidelines §6.7: את העיר צרו reads "they
    besieged the city" (צוּר), the very opposite. Same root (the guidelines' "eṣēru = יצר"), and it shows the
    cognate of Isa 37:26 / 46:11 / 22:11 (יָצַר "planned") and Gen 2:7.
  2. šibirru = מַקֵּל־רוֹעִים (§10.4 had מַקֵּל? for ET1 to decide): the Sumerian šibir already has
    מקל־רועים (Enki and the World Order 436), and a Sumerian word takes the Hebrew of its Akkadian equivalent
    (renderings §0.3); the compound also keeps eBL's "shepherd's staff". שֵׁבֶט stays free for šabbiṭu (Gilgameš XII).
  3. malāku: G = יָעַץ, Gt = נִמְלַךְ, as in Gilgameš (OB III imallikū יועצים; VII 1 imtallikū נמלכו); so
    OBM.2 יעצו and I.9 נמלכו show the stems' difference. mitluku = נִמְלָךְ (Gilgameš II 30).
  4. nadû in uššī nadû = הניח (Gilgameš I 21), not the gated הִשְׁלִיךְ.

Parallels index (ET1)

Line Source Hebrew rendering Bible Tag Comment
OBM.2 ušbū imlikū milikša mātam ישבו, יעצו את עצתה – את הארץ זֹאת הָעֵצָה הַיְּעוּצָה עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ (ישעיהו יד:כו) equivalent milik māti malāku = "the counsel counselled concerning the land": the same phrase; a sitting council of gods against the one God's counsel.
OBM.2 imlikū (malāku) יעצו / נמלכו (I.9) וַיִּמָּלֵךְ לִבִּי עָלַי (נחמיה ה:ז) cognate G = יָעַץ, Gt = נִמְלַךְ (Gilgameš).
OBM.3 bānû kibrātim בוני קצות (הארץ) בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ (בראשית א:א) divergence The gods "build" (banû) the world's edges and "set" its form; Foster's "creators" would invite בָּרָא (reserved).
OBM.5 isinnam ana nišī išīmū חג – לאנשים – גזרו וְהָיוּ לְאֹתֹת וּלְמוֹעֲדִים (בראשית א:יד); מוֹעֲדֵי יְהוָה אֲשֶׁר תִּקְרְאוּ אֹתָם מִקְרָאֵי קֹדֶשׁ (ויקרא כג:ב) equivalent Festival times decreed from above for people. Foster's "holy day" is not in the text (isinnu = festival; the root קדש reserved).
OBM.6 šarram lā iškunū מלך לא שָׂמוּ שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ (דברים יז:טו); עַתָּה שִׂימָה לָּנוּ מֶלֶךְ לְשָׁפְטֵנוּ כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם (שמואל א ח:ה) equivalent The same idiom "set a king" (šakānu = שָׂם); in the Bible the people ask, here the gods have not yet given. Also I.12.
OBM.7 ina šiātim lā kaṣrat kubšum meānum בָּהּ – לא קשורה מצנפת, עטרה וְכֹל שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִהְיֶה בָאָרֶץ (בראשית ב:ה) divergence Statives, not "not yet": Foster's "Then no headdress had been …" / "Nor yet" (8) manufacture טֶרֶם (reserved). The shared structure is real: a world lacking one office, filled from above.
OBM.7 kubšum meānum מצנפת, עטרה הָסִיר הַמִּצְנֶפֶת וְהָרִים הָעֲטָרָה (יחזקאל כא:לא) equivalent The same pair of royal insignia, given and taken by the god. Also OBM.11.
OBM.8 u haṭṭum uqniam lā ṣaprat ושרביט – ספיר לא משובץ לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה וּמְחֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו (בראשית מט:י) equivalent The sceptre as the sign of rule; ḫaṭṭu = שַׁרְבִיט, שֵׁבֶט kept for šabbiṭu. Also I.14.
OBM.8 uqniam ספיר כְּמַעֲשֵׂה לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר (שמות כד:י) equivalent Lapis lazuli = the biblical סַפִּיר.
OBM.10 sebetta bābū uddulū eli dapnim שבעה שערים – נעולים על העריץ שְׂאוּ שְׁעָרִים רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְהִנָּשְׂאוּ פִּתְחֵי עוֹלָם וְיָבוֹא מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד (תהלים כד:ז) divergence Our proposal: there the gates open to the king, here they are bolted against any would-be strongman (dapnu = Gilgameš's העריץ).
OBM.11 šibirrum מקל־רועים רְעֵה עַמְּךָ בְשִׁבְטֶךָ צֹאן נַחֲלָתֶךָ (מיכה ז:יד); שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי (תהלים כג:ד) equivalent The shepherd's staff among the royal insignia.
OBM.13 ul ibašši mitlukum ana nišīša אין נִמְלָךְ ⟨ל⟩אנשיה בְּאֵין תַּחְבֻּלוֹת יִפָּל-עָם וּתְשׁוּעָה בְּרֹב יוֹעֵץ (משלי יא:יד) equivalent A people without counsel; in Hebrew נִמְלָךְ also sounds "king" (מלך) – a Hebrew bonus, noted as such.
OBM.14 [šar]rūtum ina šamāʾī urdam [המל]כות – מן השמים ירדה וַיֵּרֶד יְהוָה לִרְאֹת אֶת הָעִיר וְאֶת הַמִּגְדָּל אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ בְּנֵי הָאָדָם (בראשית יא:ה) cognate warādu / יָרַד; [divergence]: in Gen 11 God comes down to stop a human city, here kingship comes down to a city the gods planned. The Sumerian King List's idiom ("when kingship was lowered from heaven, kingship was in Kiš"). Reading šarrūtum (collation, eBL), not Wilcke's bēltum "the Lady (Ištar) came down".
OBM.14 (the first kingship after the flood) – וְכוּשׁ יָלַד אֶת נִמְרֹד הוּא הֵחֵל לִהְיוֹת גִּבֹּר בָּאָרֶץ (בראשית י:ח); וַתְּהִי רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ בָּבֶל וְאֶרֶךְ וְאַכַּד וְכַלְנֵה בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר (בראשית י:י) divergence Genesis's first post-flood kingdom is a human "mighty one" who "began" it, not a gift from heaven. Cush = Kiš is a scholarly proposal, in the apparatus only. מַמְלָכָה reserved.
OBM.14 urdam ירדה הֵם הִמְלִיכוּ וְלֹא מִמֶּנִּי (הושע ח:ד) divergence Kingship must come from above; in Hosea the people crown kings themselves.
OBM.a+1 leqē-[ma?] קַח […] וְלָקַחְתָּ אִשָּׁה לִבְנִי לְיִצְחָק (בראשית כד:ד) cognate leqû / לָקַח; the marriage idiom only if the object is a wife (a+2, a+6): our cautious proposal.
I.1 āla īṣirū את העיר יָצְרוּ מִימֵי קֶדֶם וִיצַרְתִּיהָ עַתָּה הֲבֵאתִיהָ (ישעיהו לז:כו); יָצַרְתִּי אַף אֶעֱשֶׂנָּה (ישעיהו מו:יא) cognate eṣēru "draw, plan" = יָצַר "plan beforehand" in the god's mouth. The incipit is also the series' name.
I.1 īṣirū יָצְרוּ וַיִּיצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ז) cognate The same root for the god's first act; here its first object is a city.
I.1 āla īṣirū את העיר יָצְרוּ הָבָה נִבְנֶה לָּנוּ עִיר (בראשית יא:ד) divergence In Gen 11 humans plan and build a city and God stops them; here the city is the gods' plan from the start.
I.2 [uššīšu] iddû [את אֻשֶּׁיהָ] הניחו יְהַב אֻשַּׁיָּא דִּי בֵית אֱלָהָא דִּי בִירוּשְׁלֶם (עזרא ה:טז) cognate uššu → Aramaic אֻשַּׁיָּא; the same idiom "lay the foundations". Also I.4 (Ezra 4:12 וְאֻשַּׁיָּא יַחִיטוּ).
I.5 libna[ssu] לְבֵנָתָהּ וַתְּהִי לָהֶם הַלְּבֵנָה לְאָבֶן (בראשית יא:ג) cognate libittu / לְבֵנָה; [divergence]: the gods (the Igigi) set the city's bricks.
I.5 ukinnū כּוֹנְנוּ אֱלֹהִים יְכוֹנְנֶהָ עַד-עוֹלָם (תהלים מח:ט) equivalent The god establishes his city.
I.6 [amī]lu? lū rēʾûšin[a] [אד]ם? – יהי רוֹעָן יִפְקֹד יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי הָרוּחֹת לְכָל בָּשָׂר אִישׁ עַל הָעֵדָה (במדבר כז:טז); וְלֹא תִהְיֶה עֲדַת יְהוָה כַּצֹּאן אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהֶם רֹעֶה (במדבר כז:יז); וְהוּא יִהְיֶה לָהֶן לְרֹעֶה (יחזקאל לד:כג) equivalent "A man" appointed as shepherd; Ezekiel has even the feminine plural suffix (-šina / לָהֶן).
I.6 [amī]lu? lū rēʾûšin[a] [אד]ם? – יהי רוֹעָן וְאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ה); וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יָצָר (בראשית ב:ח) divergence Our proposal: in both beginnings "a man" is missing for an office, and the deity "forms" (יָצַר / eṣēru, I.1) and "sets" (שָׂם / šakānu, OBM.6): to work the ground there, to shepherd the people here.
I.7 e[t]ana lū itinšina אֵ[תָ]נָה – יהי בַּנָּאָן וַיְהִי בֹּנֶה עִיר וַיִּקְרָא שֵׁם הָעִיר כְּשֵׁם בְּנוֹ חֲנוֹךְ (בראשית ד:יז) equivalent Our proposal: city, builder, son, name – the elements of Etana's story (his quest for a son, "establish a name for me", II.142). The name explained by a role (Etana / itinnu) as קַיִן / קָנִיתִי (בראשית ד:א).
I.7 itinnu בַּנָּאָן וַיִּבֶן אֶת נִינְוֵה וְאֶת רְחֹבֹת עִיר וְאֶת כָּלַח (בראשית י:יא) equivalent The first kings after the flood as city builders.
I.13 ina ūmīšū-ma ביום ההוא בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו יַעֲשֶׂה (שופטים יז:ו) equivalent "In those days" + "no king". OB has ina šiātim בָּהּ (OBM.7).
I.13 ina ūmīšū-ma ביום ההוא בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם (בראשית ב:ד) divergence The "on the day when" opening before the description of what is lacking (Gen 2:5) – but with no "not yet".
I.19 ištar rēʾâ … (I.20) u šarra išeʾʾi אִשְׁתַּר – רועה … ומלך – מבקשת בִּקֵּשׁ יְהוָה לוֹ אִישׁ כִּלְבָבוֹ וַיְצַוֵּהוּ יְהוָה לְנָגִיד עַל עַמּוֹ (שמואל א יג:יד); וְהִנֵּה רֹעֶה בַּצֹּאן (שמואל א טז:יא); וַיִּבְחַר בְּדָוִד עַבְדּוֹ וַיִּקָּחֵהוּ מִמִּכְלְאֹת צֹאן (תהלים עח:ע) equivalent The deity "seeks" a shepherd who will be king (šeʾû = בִּקֵּשׁ). Foster's "came down from heaven to seek" (I.19, 21) is a restoration resting on the abandoned reading bēltum in OBM 14. Also I.21–22.
I.23 enlil ihâṭ parakki šamê אֶנְלִיל בוחן את דוכן השמים יְהוָה בַּשָּׁמַיִם כִּסְאוֹ עֵינָיו יֶחֱזוּ עַפְעַפָּיו יִבְחֲנוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם (תהלים יא:ד) equivalent A throne in heaven and a god who "examines".

I.a+2 [mar]hīssu ana šâšū-m[a] [רעי]יתו אליו וַתָּבֹא הָאִשָּׁה וַתֹּאמֶר לְאִישָׁהּ (שופטים יג:ו) divergence The (barren, 13:2) wife of Manoah tells her husband of a revelation that ends in a son; here the wife of a sonless king tells a dream. [absent]: no woman dreams in the Hebrew Bible.

I.a+7 eṭemmašu אִטּוֹ אֵין לִי בֵן בַּעֲבוּר הַזְכִּיר שְׁמִי (שמואל ב יח:יח) equivalent The sonless man's care for his name after death; [absent] the Torah has no cult of the ghost (אֱלֹהִים רָאִיתִי עֹלִים מִן הָאָרֶץ, שמואל א כח:יג, only through the forbidden אוֹב).

Key findings

The Bible.

  1. The opening is not a "when not yet" opening. OBM 7–9 are statives ("not bound", "not set", "not built");
    Foster's "Then no headdress had been …", "Nor yet" import the טֶרֶם of Gen 2:5. What is shared is the structure:
    a world that lacks one office ("no man to work the ground" / "no king"), filled from above by a god who "forms"
    (eṣēru = יָצַר, I.1; Gen 2:7) and "sets" (šakānu = שָׂם, OBM.6; Gen 2:8).
  2. Gen 11 inverted. In Etana the gods plan the city (eṣēru = יָצַר, the "planning" of Isa 37:26, 46:11), lay
    its foundations (uššu, the source of Aramaic אֻשַּׁיָּא, Ezra 5:16 – the same idiom) and set its bricks (libittu
    = לְבֵנָה, Gen 11:3), and then kingship "comes down" (warādu = יָרַד). In Gen 11 humans plan and build, and God
    "comes down" (11:5) to stop them. Gen 10:8–10 makes the first post-flood kingdom a human achievement (הֵחֵל,
    גִּבֹּר), where the Sumerian King List and Etana have kingship lowered from heaven to Kiš (Cush = Kiš only as a
    proposal).
  3. The vocabulary of kingship is shared: "set a king" (šarram šakānu = שׂוּם מֶלֶךְ, Deut 17:15, 1 Sam 8:5); the
    kingless "in those days" (SB I.13; Judg 17:6, 21:25); the insignia pair מִצְנֶפֶת / עֲטָרָה (Ezek 21:31); the
    shepherd's staff (Mic 7:14, Ps 23:4); "a man as their shepherd" (I.6; Num 27:16–17; Ezek 34:23 with the same
    feminine plural suffix); the deity who "seeks" a shepherd-king (I.19–22; 1 Sam 13:14, 16:11, Ps 78:70–71); the god
    who "examines" from his throne in heaven (I.23; Ps 11:4); "the counsel counselled concerning the land" (OBM.2; Isa
    14:26).
  4. A builder without a son. I.7 calls Etana the people's "builder" (itinnu, a play on his name); Gen 4:17's first
    city-builder names the city after his son. Etana's story will turn on the son he does not have (II.140–142 "establish
    a name for me"); the wife's dream (I.a+2–a+7) mentions "his ghost", whose care needs a son (2 Sam 18:18 Absalom).
  5. False echoes avoided (rank-3 English): "holy day" (isinnu = חַג), "Then … had not / Nor yet" (statives),
    "creators" (bānû "builders", not בָּרָא), "right counsel", "four world regions" (I.10: an old restoration),
    "came down from heaven to seek" (I.19, 21: a restoration resting on the abandoned bēltum), "with ramparts" (I.18),
    "instead of" (kīma, I.a+4–a+5). The reading [šar]rūtum (OBM.14, collation) removes Ištar's descent from heaven.

The ancient mind.

  1. The city before the king. The gods plan the city, lay its foundations and bricks (the Igigi, the labouring gods
    of Atra-ḫasīs) and surround it (I.18); the world already has edges, form, people and a festival. Only kingship is
    missing – and it is not a human invention but an object kept "before Anu in heaven" (OBM.11–12): sceptre, tiara,
    turban, shepherd's staff.
  2. Kingship cannot be seized. "Seven gates are bolted against the aggressive one" (OBM.10): no strongman can take
    it; it must be lowered (OBM.14, the Sumerian King List's idiom). The SB rereads the number as the Seven gods (the
    Sebetti) who bar the gates against "the multitude" and "the settlements" (I.16–17) – the whole of humankind shut out.
  3. The king's two faces: shepherd and builder (I.6–7) – the leader of the human flock and the builder of the city
    and its temples, the two roles of every Mesopotamian royal inscription; the name Etana explained by itinnu.
  4. The goddess chooses: Ištar/Innina "seeks" a shepherd and a king, as she "loved" Sargon; Enlil inspects the dais
    of heaven – a coronation prepared above before a king is found below. The festival (OBM.5) is "decreed" with the same
    verb as fate: joy is part of humanity's lot.
  5. A wife's dream: dreams are "shown" by a god (barû Š), and women dream and interpret (Ninsun, the women of the
    Mari letters); the dream concerns Etana, "their death?" and "his ghost" – the dead who need a son to pour water for
    them (Gilgameš XII 152).
  6. The scribes: the incipit āla īṣirū is the series' title in the Nineveh colophons (Langdon 1931 read "the city
    they hated"); the SB copyist wrote kibrāti by mistake in I.15, carried over from I.10 – writing from memory.

Open decisions (numbered; the minor ones decided)

  1. eṣēru = יָצְרוּ instead of guidelines §6.7's צָר (decided; reason above). The coordinator may add to §6.7:
    "צָר for drawing images; the full יָצַר where צר could read צוּר 'besiege'".
  2. ḫaṭṭu across corpora (lead): שַׁרְבִיט here (renderings §10.4; Gilgameš VIII 128, 153; Sum. ĝidru in the
    laments and Gudea), but Enūma eliš IV 29 and LH (prologue 161, epilogue 3187′, 3356′, 3392′) give ḫaṭṭu / GIDRU
    שֵׁבֶט – while Gilgameš XII 19, 39 give שֵׁבֶט to its cognate šabbiṭu. Proposal: ḫaṭṭu = שַׁרְבִיט everywhere,
    שֵׁבֶט only for šabbiṭu.
  3. parakku (lead): כֵּס (Etana II, here; EA barag) vs Enūma eliš דוכן (V 115; VI 51, 53, 58, 68, 118). Settled 2026-10-23 (../../harmonization--2026-10-23.md row 5): דּוּכָן.
  4. meānu עֲטָרָה (§10.4) vs Enki and the World Order 264, Sum. aga עטרת (= Akk. agû, כֶּתֶר in Gilgameš):
    EWO's aga should probably be כֶּתֶר (lead). kubšu מִצְנֶפֶת = Sum. saĝšu מצנפת (EA 578) – consistent; but
    Enūma eliš VII 8 has מצנפתו for šukūssu (italic) – a minor split.
  5. ṣapāru משובץ collides with Gilgameš VIII 170, 185 raʾzu משובץ (both uncertain, both italic). Kept
    (decided): it is the natural Hebrew for a stone set in metal, and both renderings are marked uncertain; alternatives
    tried and rejected: קבוע (EA us₂; reads "permanent"), מוטבע (LH/EST ṭebû = טבע), משוקע (šabāḫu).
  6. barû Š and kullumu both הֶרְאָה (renderings §10.3 sets both; flood: XI 197 הראיתי חלום; Gilgameš OB
    הַרְאֵנִי): a pre-set double mapping. Left (natural Hebrew for both); ET4 should note it where both occur (coordinator).
  7. ḫiāṭu בָּחַן (Gilgameš I 19, 41) vs Enūma eliš barû בוחן (IV 65, 135; VII 35) and the wisdom corpus
    bārû הַבּוֹחֵן: an existing collision; I followed Gilgameš (lead).
  8. ina ūmīšū-ma ביום ההוא (Gilgameš III 95, VIII 41) vs בעת ההיא (Enūma eliš IV 63, Adapa, the Founding of
    Eridu): I followed Gilgameš (lead may harmonize).
  9. OBM.7 ina šiātim = בָּהּ (decided): literal "in it/her", leaving open eBL's "at that (time)" and Streck's "in it
    (the land) = here".
  10. OBM.13 mitlukum = נִמְלָךְ (decided; Gilgameš II 30): fits both the adjective "circumspect" and the
    infinitive "deliberation"; הִמָּלְכוּת was rejected because unvocalized it reads המלכות "the kingship" (OBM.14).
  11. I.24 מבקשת ומבקשת (decided): feminine, continuing Ištar's verb (I.20, 22); the subject may be Enlil (I.23).
  12. The formula X ana šâšū-ma ana Y izzakaršu = X אליו, אל Y, דיבר: (I.a+2, decided): for ET4 (III b+15,
    b+26, b+32, b+36 → הנשר אליו, אל אֵתָנָה, דיבר:). A FORMULAS regex could be added (coordinator).
  13. I.4 brackets (decided): האל[ים? per the ATF (DINGIR#-[MEŠ?), although eBL's N brackets the whole word.
  14. OBM.a+1–a+13 and I.a+2–a+7: whether OB Morgan col. ii tells Etana's marriage, and whether it is the same scene
    as SB I a+2, cannot be decided from the fragments; the notes say "perhaps" only.

Deviations from renderings §10 (decided at the first occurrence, with the reason)

  1. bâru = לָכַד (not §10.3's צָד): one Hebrew per source word across corpora – the Gilgameš corpus has bâru
    = לָכַד (OB Ishchali 15' צפור לכוד); צָד is the cognate of ṣâdu / ṣayyādu (Gilgameš צייד); and the sense
    is "catch, trap (with a net)" (eBL). It also makes the idiom of the net exact: רשת שַׁמַשׁ תלכדך (II.47) ↔
    וְרִשְׁתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר-טָמַן תִּלְכְּדוֹ (תהלים לה:ח). No FORMULAS regex involves it; only the prose of §10.3 changes
    (… – הנחש לוכד,; רשת שַׁמַשׁ תלכדך). Note: Gilgameš itself also has ḫābilu לוכד (I 111, VII 94) – a
    Gilgameš-internal near-collision (participle of לכד for ḫābilu, finite verbs for bâru).
  2. nērebu = מָבוֹא (not §10.3's מַעֲבָר, which is Gilgameš's nēberu, X 79, XI 248); nērebtu = מְבוֹאָה
    (OBS 2, MA b+3; מְבוֹאֹת יָם, יחזקאל כז:ג).
  3. qerbetu = נָוֶה (Gilgameš VIII 13 qerbētu הנאות); OBS a+20 רשתך – הַנָּוֶה הרחב.
  4. The animals (§10.4 left them to ET2): turāḫu = יָעֵל (= Sum. dara₂ / taraḫ, יעל in EA 182 and Agade 23),
    so §10.4's יָעֵל? for armu moves: armu (eBL "mountain goat"; ≠ arwiu / armû "male gazelle", צבי in the
    love songs) = אַקּוֹ (pl. אַקּוֹאִים); ditānu = תְּאוֹ (pl. תְּאוֹאִים; = Sum. alim, תְּאוֹ in Gudea, EWO,
    Agade; §10.4's תְּאוֹ? for turāḫu would have collided); sappāru = זֶמֶר (pl. זְמָרִים, always vocalized);
    mindinu = בַּרְדְּלָס (Gilgameš); nimru = נָמֵר; rīmu רְאֵם; serrēmu חמור בר (Gilgameš string,
    without maqaf; §10.4 has חֲמוֹר־בָּר); ṣabītu צְבִיָּה.
  5. mullû ina qāti: II.50's restored [umalli] is formally D preterite (present would be umalla); kept as §10.3's
    present ימסרהו., with a note.

II.43 ina šamāmī uššab ובשמים אשב וּמִגְדָּל וְרֹאשׁוֹ בַשָּׁמַיִם (בראשית יא:ד) divergence Ascent to heaven out of pride, but by a bird's wings, not a tower.
II.44 akkal inba ואוכל תנובה וַתִּקַּח מִפִּרְיוֹ וַתֹּאכַל (בראשית ג:ו) divergence Our proposal: a creature that wants a god's life and eats from the tree; inbu = תְּנוּבָה, never פְּרִי (Gilgameš).
II.45 atmu ṣehru atar hasīsa האפרוח הקטן, יתיר־התבונה אֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ בֵיצִים (דברים כב:ו) equivalent watmu = אֶפְרוֹחַ; גּוֹזָל (דברים לב:יא) reserved. The epithet is Atra-ḫasīs's name. Identical in OBS.22, MA.c+3.
II.45 (the wise child) יתיר־התבונה מִפִּי עוֹלְלִים וְיֹנְקִים יִסַּדְתָּ עֹז (תהלים ח:ג) equivalent Wisdom in the mouth of the smallest.
II.47 šētu ša šamaš ibâr[ka] רשת שַׁמַשׁ תלכד[ך] וּפָרַשְׂתִּי אֶת רִשְׁתִּי עָלָיו וְנִתְפַּשׂ בִּמְצוּדָתִי (יחזקאל יב:יג); אָלָתִי אֲשֶׁר בָּזָה וּבְרִיתִי אֲשֶׁר הֵפִיר (יחזקאל יז:יט) equivalent The god's net spread over the oath-breaker.
II.47 šētu ša šamaš רשת שַׁמַשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵלֵכוּ אֶפְרוֹשׂ עֲלֵיהֶם רִשְׁתִּי כְּעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם אוֹרִידֵם (הושע ז:יב) equivalent The divine net brings the bird down from the sky – the eagle's fate. Also II.70.
II.48 gišparru … ibarrūnikk[a] הפח … וילכדוך הֲיַעֲלֶה פַּח מִן הָאֲדָמָה וְלָכוֹד לֹא יִלְכּוֹד (עמוס ג:ה) equivalent Trap + לכד.
II.51 ul išmēšunūtī-ma … לא שמע להם, לא שמע ל[מאמר בניו?] שְׁמַע בְּנִי מוּסַר אָבִיךָ (משלי א:ח) divergence Wisdom's order reversed: the father does not listen to the son, and is punished.
II.56 qinnašu laššu וקנו איננו הַיֶּלֶד אֵינֶנּוּ וַאֲנִי אָנָה אֲנִי בָא (בראשית לז:ל) equivalent The cry over an empty place.
OBS.a+6 laššû [mārūšu?] ואינם [בניו?] רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל בָּנֶיהָ; מֵאֲנָה לְהִנָּחֵם עַל בָּנֶיהָ כִּי אֵינֶנּוּ (ירמיהו לא:יד) equivalent A parent weeping for children who are not; also OBS.a+17, II.60.
OBS.a+17 laššû mārūʾa אינם בניי יוֹסֵף אֵינֶנּוּ וְשִׁמְעוֹן אֵינֶנּוּ (בראשית מב:לו) equivalent Jacob's lament.
II.61 ana pān šamaš i[llakā dimāšu] לפני שַׁמַשׁ – [זולגות דמעותיו] מְלִיצַי רֵעָי; אֶל-אֱלוֹהַּ דָּלְפָה עֵינִי (איוב טז:כ) equivalent Friends betray, the tears flow to the god. זולגות דמעותיו = Gilgameš's string for illakā dimāšu. Also OBS.a+10.
II.62 atkalkum-ma šamaš [qurādu] בך בטחתי, שַׁמַשׁ [הגיבור] אֱלֹהַי בְּךָ בָטַחְתִּי אַל-אֵבוֹשָׁה (תהלים כה:ב) equivalent The opening of an individual lament; the whole speech (II.62–72, OBS.a+11–24) has the psalm structure: trust, innocence, complaint, "you know", the god's power, plea for punishment.
OBS.a+12 ana erîm ramānī anāku ašruk לנשר – את עצמי – אני הֶעֱנַקְתִּי גַּם-אִישׁ שְׁלוֹמִי אֲשֶׁר-בָּטַחְתִּי בוֹ אוֹכֵל לַחְמִי הִגְדִּיל עָלַי עָקֵב (תהלים מא:י) equivalent The trusted friend who ate of mine and betrayed.
OBS.a+13 ādur-ma nīška ukabbit חרדתי, ואת חַיֶּיךָ כיבדתי וְאֶת-יִרְאֵי יְהוָה יְכַבֵּד; נִשְׁבַּע לְהָרַע וְלֹא יָמִר (תהלים טו:ד) equivalent Honouring the oath by the god's life; kabātu D / כִּבֵּד [cognate]. Foster's "you" hides the oath (nīšu).
OBS.a+14 lemuttam ul ukīl ana ibrīya רעה לא החזקתי לרֵעִי אַל-תַּחֲרֹשׁ עַל-רֵעֲךָ רָעָה; וְהוּא-יוֹשֵׁב לָבֶטַח אִתָּךְ (משלי ג:כט) equivalent The serpent kept the precept, the eagle broke it (OBS.a+24, II.72 מחזיק רעה לרֵעֵהוּ).
OBS.a+15 šū qinnašu šalim-ma sapih qin[nī] הוא – קנו שלם, ופזור קני מַדּוּעַ דֶּרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים צָלֵחָה שָׁלוּ כָּל בֹּגְדֵי בָגֶד (ירמיהו יב:א) equivalent The traitor whole, the faithful ruined: the righteous sufferer's complaint inside a fable.
II.66 saphū atmūʾa פזורים אפרוחיי פֶּן נָפוּץ עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ (בראשית יא:ד) equivalent sapāḫu is the Akkadian "scatter"; פּוּץ / הֵפִיץ reserved for Gen 11, so פָּזוּר. Foster's "while his young are safe" rests on a reading eBL's collation excludes.
II.68 lumna ša īpušanni šama[š lū tīde] את הרוע אשר עשה לי – שַׁמַשׁ, [אָכֵן יָדַעְתָּ] וְאַתָּה יְהוָה יָדַעְתָּ אֶת כָּל עֲצָתָם עָלַי לַמָּוֶת (ירמיהו יח:כג) equivalent "You know" + the plea for punishment. Also OBS.a+19 (OB: "the evil that came to me").
II.69 šētka erṣ[etu rapaštu] רשתך – הארץ [הרחבה] אִם אֶסַּק שָׁמַיִם שָׁם אָתָּה; וְאַצִּיעָה שְּׁאוֹל הִנֶּךָּ (תהלים קלט:ח) equivalent No escape from the god, heaven or earth (II.69–70).
II.69 šētka erṣetu / gišparraka šamû רשתך – הארץ … פַּחְךָ – השמים אִם יַחְתְּרוּ בִשְׁאוֹל מִשָּׁם יָדִי תִקָּחֵם; וְאִם יַעֲלוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם מִשָּׁם אוֹרִידֵם (עמוס ט:ב); מִשָּׁם אֲצַוֶּה אֶת הַנָּחָשׁ וּנְשָׁכָם (עמוס ט:ג) equivalent Heaven and earth, and the serpent as the god's agent of punishment – exactly the sequel (ET3; MA.c+24).
II.69 šētka erṣetu רשתך – הארץ הֲתִפֹּל צִפּוֹר עַל פַּח הָאָרֶץ (עמוס ג:ה) equivalent "The trap of the earth".
OBS.a+20 šētka qerbetum rap[aštum] רשתך – הַנָּוֶה הר[חב] יִרְעֶה מִקְנֶיךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כַּר נִרְחָב (ישעיהו ל:כג) equivalent "A wide pasture": the same phrase (other Hebrew noun). OB's net is the pasture around the town; SB's (II.69) the whole earth.
II.71 ina šētīka ai uṣ[i erû] מרשתך אל יצא [הנשר] נַפְשֵׁנוּ כְּצִפּוֹר נִמְלְטָה מִפַּח יוֹקְשִׁים (תהלים קכד:ז) divergence There the righteous bird escapes the trap; here the wronged one prays that the wicked bird will not. Also OBS.a+22.
II.72 ēpiš lemutti anzû mukī[l lemutti ana ibrīšu] עושה רעה, אַנְזוּ – מחזיק [רעה לרֵעֵהוּ] וְאִישׁ אֶת רָעַת רֵעֵהוּ אַל תַּחְשְׁבוּ בִּלְבַבְכֶם וּשְׁבֻעַת שֶׁקֶר אַל תֶּאֱהָבוּ (זכריה ח:יז) equivalent Evil against the friend and a false oath, together. OB (OBS.a+23) has anzillu תועבה where SB has the mythical bird Anzû.
OBS.1 lihliqšum ṭūdum ai uta harrānam יאבד לו הנתיב, אל ימצא אוֹרַח וְגָדַרְתִּי אֶת גְּדֵרָהּ וּנְתִיבוֹתֶיהָ לֹא תִמְצָא (הושע ב:ח) equivalent "Her paths she shall not find": ai uta = לֹא תִמְצָא, ṭūdu = נָתִיב. Also אָרְחִי גָדַר וְלֹא אֶעֱבוֹר (איוב יט:ח).
OBS.4 māmītam uttamammû שבועה – נשבעו זה לזה וַיִּשָּׁבְעוּ אִישׁ לְאָחִיו (בראשית כו:לא) equivalent A reciprocal oath (Dt/Rt).
MA.b+5 rēssu lišši את ראשו יִשָּׂא בְּעוֹד שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים יִשָּׂא פַרְעֹה אֶת רֹאשְׁךָ מֵעָלֶיךָ (בראשית מ:יט) equivalent rēša našû "single out" = נָשָׂא רֹאשׁ, an idiom kept literal: for grace (Gen 40:13) or death (40:19); here death. MA only.
MA.b+11 irtūʾūni התרועעו אִישׁ רֵעִים לְהִתְרֹעֵעַ (משלי יח:כד) cognate râʾu / רעה "befriend" (Prov 22:24 אַל-תִּתְרַע); rūʾu (עָמִית) is the same Semitic root as רֵעַ, hidden by the Gilgameš rendering.
MA.b+13 nazmat kabtātīšunu iptašrūni את צרות כְּבֵדֵיהֶם – פָּשְׁרוּ זה לזה אֲשֶׁר יַחְדָּו נַמְתִּיק סוֹד (תהלים נה:טו) equivalent The friend who shared one's secrets and betrayed (Ps 55:13–21). Foster's "desires" is not nazmātu "troubles".
MA.c+5 [ṣerru rabiṣ] [הנחש רובץ] לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ (בראשית ד:ז) cognate rabāṣu / רבץ: the lurker (cf. the rābiṣu demon). Restored from SB II.100.
MA.c+6 erṣetu iṣṣ[a]na[bbatka?] הארץ – [תתפסך?] וַתִּפְתַּח הָאָרֶץ אֶת פִּיהָ וַתִּבְלַע אֹתָם (במדבר טז:לב) equivalent The earth that seizes the sinner; Foster's "netherworld" is interpretation. Restored. Also MA.c+9.
MA.c+16 išni … / ušalliš … שָׁנָה … / שִׁלֵּשׁ … וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁנוּ וַיִּשְׁנוּ וַיֹּאמֶר שַׁלֵּשׁוּ וַיְשַׁלֵּשׁוּ (מלכים א יח:לד) cognate šanû / שָׁנָה, šalāšu / שִׁלֵּשׁ: "a second, a third time" (c+14–18).
MA.c+24 ṣerru iṣṣabassu הנחש תפס אותו מִשָּׁם אֲצַוֶּה אֶת הַנָּחָשׁ וּנְשָׁכָם (עמוס ט:ג) equivalent The serpent as the god's instrument of punishment.
MA.c+29 [d]ayyān dīni דיין הדין הֲשֹׁפֵט כָּל הָאָרֶץ לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט (בראשית יח:כה) equivalent Šamaš as judge; dayyānu / dīnu = דַּיָּן / דִּין [cognate].

Key findings

The Bible.

  1. The oath of friendship is told as a treaty, and it meets Genesis's oath scenes word for word: alka nīpuša
    rūʾūta … anāku u kâši     (II.8–9) = Laban's לְכָה נִכְרְתָה בְרִית אֲנִי וָאָתָּה (Gen 31:44); māmīta itmû
    kilallān     (II.16, 23) = כִּי שָׁם נִשְׁבְּעוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם (Gen 21:31); the reciprocal oath (OBS.4) = וַיִּשָּׁבְעוּ אִישׁ לְאָחִיו (Gen 26:31); the conditional lemnētā-ma "if you are evil" (II.12) = אִם תַּעֲשֵׂה עִמָּנוּ רָעָה (Gen 26:29); "Šamaš's boundary" (II.17, 19, 49) = Laban's heap that neither may cross (Gen 31:52) and the
    cursed mover of the friend's boundary (Deut 19:14, 27:17). The oath ends in curses, like Deut 28.
  2. Isa 14:13 is the eagle's plan: "I will go up and dwell in heaven" (II.43; OBS.19–20) has the same two verbs, in
    the same order and person, both cognates, and in both the thought is "in the heart" (II.37; OBS.14). Obad 1:4 / Jer
    49:16 add the eagle's nest among the stars and the god who brings it down. Gen 11:4 is a [divergence] (pride and
    ascent, but no tower); the "tower" of II.2 (dimtu) is an uncertain sign in a broken line beside a shrine of
    Adad, not a Gen 11 parallel     (rendered צְרִיחַ, מִגְדָּל reserved).
  3. The net of the divine judge: choosing bâru = לָכַד (Gilgameš) makes II.47 רשת שַׁמַשׁ תלכדך the exact idiom
    of Ps 35:8 (net + לכד; Ps 9:16, Amos 3:5). Ezekiel 17 is the closest structural parallel to the whole fable: an
    eagle, a צַפְצָפָה (17:5), a broken oath (17:13–19) and the god's net (17:20; 12:13). Hos 7:12 (the net that brings
    the birds down from the sky), Ps 139:8 and Amos 9:2–3 (no escape in heaven or earth – and the god commands the
    serpent to bite) match "your net is the wide earth, your trap the distant heaven" (II.69–70) and the sequel (ET3).
  4. The eagle's crime is eating: the serpent's condition calls breaking the friendship "eating a taboo" (II.13,
    asakka akālu) – the idiom of לֹא תֹאכַל כָּל תּוֹעֵבָה (Deut 14:3) – and the eagle breaks it by literally
    eating. The bird's-nest law (Deut 22:6–7) has the same verb for the brooding mother (rabiṣ / רֹבֶצֶת, II.5); the
    eagle does what the law forbids in spirit.
  5. The serpent is the righteous one: against Gen 3:1 (the cunning serpent among חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה), here the serpent
    is faithful, generous ("I gave myself to the eagle"), God-fearing ("I honoured your life" = the oath, cf. Ps 15:4),
    and its lament has the structure of a biblical individual lament (Ps 25:2, Jer 18:23, Jer 12:1, Job 16:20, Ps
    41:10). The eagle is the one who "harbours evil against his friend" (Prov 3:29, Zech 8:17).
  6. False echoes avoided (rank-3 English): Foster's "tower" (II.2), "netherworld" (II.15, MA.c+6, c+9), "curse" for
    māmītu (II.22), "desires" (MA.b+13), "No doubt" for minde "perhaps" (MA.c+5), "king of the gods" for šar
    ša[mê]     (MA.c+28), "you" for nīška (OBS.a+13), and the restoration "while his young are safe" (II.66), which
    eBL's collation excludes. mullû ina qāti is never מִלֵּא יָד.

The ancient mind.

  1. Friendship as a sworn treaty under the sun-god: two animals swear "before Šamaš the warrior" and by the earth;
    the curses are those of state treaties – lost paths, closed passes, a roving weapon, Šamaš's trap, and (MA only)
    being "singled out for the slaughterer" and a gallû demon riding on one's back. The god who sees everything is the
    guarantor of every oath, and the broken oath itself becomes the trap (gišparru māmīt šamaš).
  2. The three versions show a growing cosmos: OB's net is "the wide pasture" around the settlement (OBS.a+20), SB's
    "the wide earth" and "the distant heaven" (II.69–70): the shepherds' world became the universe. SB also makes the
    hunt reciprocal (eagle and serpent alternate, II.26–33), where OB and MA have the serpent alone hunting – the
    betrayal of a fully mutual friendship.
  3. Intimacy and its betrayal: MA alone describes the friendship from inside – "they befriended each other, became
    (as) twins, partners, unburdened the troubles of their livers to each other" (MA.b+11–13). The eagle's plan comes
    when his young have grown and left the nest (OBS.15–17).
  4. The wise child and the deaf father: the littlest fledgling bears Atra-ḫasīs's name ("exceedingly wise"), quotes
    the oath word for word (II.47–50), and is not heard (II.51) – the flood hero's role in a family drama.
  5. A parent's grief: the serpent comes home carrying meat for his friend (II.54), finds the nest gone, weeps before
    the sun; his lament is a legal plea ("you know, Šamaš") and a cry ("his nest is whole, mine scattered; his
    fledglings safe, my children are not").
  6. SB rewrote anzillu "abomination" as Anzû (II.72 vs OBS.a+23): the eagle becomes the monstrous bird who stole
    the Tablet of Destinies – a creature that grasped at the gods' power, as the eagle wanted to "dwell in heaven".

Open decisions (numbered; the minor ones decided)

  1. II.25 – a tool bug, not a translation problem. eBL's reconstruction of SB II 25 is U₄.1.KAM@v.TA.AM₃ | inaṣṣarū | b[ūla] (a %sb logogram + normalized words). tools/ebl_fetch.py put its normalized half under line 24 as
    "N (variant, other manuscripts)" and left line 25's N empty, so verify ET reports "II.25: transliteration differs
    from the base text". The entry carries eBL's real reconstruction. Needs: a fix in ebl_fetch.py (keep a
    reconstruction that starts with a non-normalized logogram) and a regenerated Etana-SB-II/reading-edition.md, or an
    allow-list entry in kings_tools.py. (Coordinator; I did not touch the tools.)
  2. ḫarrānu / urḫu across corpora (coordinator / user). Renderings §10.3 has ḫarrānu = דֶּרֶךְ, urḫu =
    אֹרַח (and the ✓ formula לך באורח, חלוף את ההר for alik urḫa); the Gilgameš and wisdom corpora have the
    reverse (urḫu = דֶּרֶךְ, ḫarrānu = אֹרַח). The harmonization of 2026-10-21 lists ḫarrānu as "kept by sense",
    but urḫu is not. In my lines only OBS.1 (אל ימצא דרך), which follows §10.3. If harmonized to Gilgameš: OBS.1 →
    אל ימצא אורח, and the formula → לך בדרך, חלוף את ההר (ET3, II.75 …).
    Coordinator, 2026-10-22: harmonized to Gilgameš (urḫu = דֶּרֶךְ, ḫarrānu = אוֹרַח, vocalized): OBS.1 changed, the formula is לך בדרך, חלוף את ההר,.
  3. bâru = לָכַד instead of §10.3's צָד (decided; reason above). §10.3's prose strings need updating.
  4. nērebu = מָבוֹא, nērebtu = מְבוֹאָה, instead of §10.3's מַעֲבָר (decided).
  5. Animals (decided): armu אַקּוֹ, turāḫu יָעֵל, ditānu תְּאוֹ, sappāru זֶמֶר. Side collision found in
    another corpus: Enki and the World Order renders taraḫ (in the boat name taraḫ abzu) אקו־האפסו, while EA 182
    and the Curse of Agade render taraḫ יעל – with this decision אקו belongs to armu; the EWO boat name could
    become יעל־האפסו (creation corpus; coordinator/lead).
  6. šarāku = הֶעֱנִיק (OBS.a+12) = Sum. rig₇ (EA 614 העניק); the Gilgameš corpus also has qiāšu = הֶעֱנִיק
    – an existing cross-corpus collision (two Akkadian verbs), for the lead.
  7. nabalkutu "cross; turn over" = חָצָה for crossing a mountain (renderings §0.3) but הִתְהַפֵּךְ עַל for a trap
    that springs over its prey (II.22, 48; MA.b+1) – one lemma, two senses (decided).
  8. rūʾu עָמִית vs râʾu הִתְרוֹעֵעַ (MA.b+11): the Hebrew verb keeps the Semitic root (= רֵעַ), the noun (Gilgameš)
    does not; changing rūʾu to רֵעַ would collide with ibru רֵעַ. Kept; noted in the apparatus.
  9. II.50 [umalli] – restored, formally D preterite; rendered as §10.3's present ימסרהו. (decided; noted).
  10. lū + tīde = אָכֵן יָדַעְתָּ (II.68, OBS.a+19; renderings §2 "lū + preterite = אָכֵן"; Jer 18:23
    יָדַעְתָּ). ET3/ET4 should keep it if the phrase recurs.
  11. II.1 [קורא?] – the gated קרא licensed by nabû; the [equivalent] to Gen 2:19–20 is marked as a cautious
    proposal (the line is broken); the coordinator may drop it.

    קָרַב / נִגַּשׁ / בָּא (qerēbu, ṭeḫû, erēbu) → sanāqu בִּקֵּר; אַשְׁמָה (would make II.125 blame Šamaš) →
    šērtu עֹנֶשׁ (Atraḫasīs). Remaining cross-corpus collisions are listed under open decisions.
  • Pass (c) Hebrew: read aloud; vocalized what would otherwise be misread: אֵתָנָה (every occurrence and heading),
    שַׁמַשׁ / הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ (MA f+2), אֶתְּנָה "I will give" (II.114, OBM c+7: unvocalized it is Etana's name), מִכְסֵה הַלֵּב (not מִכְסָה "quota"), בַּמִּגְרָשִׁים, אֵילַי (not אֵלַי), שֵׂיִי, האִטִּים, שָׁתִית, יָרֵאתִי,
    גָּמְרוּ, מֻגְמָרַי, שָׁנָה (not "year"), נָסַח, קִנִּי, בָּאתָ, לֵךְ / לְךָ, רְאֵה, בְּחַן, פְּתַח,
    קְרַב, שׂוּם, אָשִׂים, שִׂים, שֵׁם, מֻשְׁבָּע, אֲבַקֶּרְךָ, הַחֲיֵנִי, אַחֲיֶה, הַעֲלֵנִי, אַעַלְךָ,
    בַּחֲצוֹתְךָ, וְהַשְׁלִיכֵהוּ, מְרֹט, כְּרֹת, הַנַּח; simplified לְּךָ → לְךָ.

Deviations from renderings §10 (decided at the first occurrence, with the reason)

  1. kutum libbi = מִכְסֵה הַלֵּב (II.83, 110), not §10.3's מכסה הקרביים: קֶרֶב (קְרָבַיִם) is the
    [cognate] of qerbu (MA c+23, II.145, 150, MA d+9, e+10), and libbu of the carcass is לֵב in every line of the
    scene (MA c+5, c+20; II.77, 84, 91, 100, 111; of the pit II.146, 151, MA d+10). The sacrificial parallel stays
    visible in the apparatus: אֶת הַחֵלֶב הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת הַקֶּרֶב (Lev 3:3).
  2. kubru = עֹבִי (II.134; Gilgameš VI 127, 136, 142, 161), not §10.3's מִשְׁמַנֵּי: one Akkadian word = one
    Hebrew word, and וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ (Gen 27:28) would be an echo without basis.
  3. šubtu = מִשְׁכָּן (II.78, 92; Gilgameš), šubta nadû = הֵנִיחַ מִשְׁכָּן (nadû "lay" = הניח, ET1) –
    Foster's "ambush" is the sense (eBL: jB šubtu also "trap"); מַאֲרָב belongs to ušbu (Gilgameš I 168).
  4. MA d+7 has etiq šadâm-ma, not šadâ ebir as §10.3 says (the tablet: e-tiq KUR-ma): so חלוף את ההר, the SB
    formula; [mā?] (restored quotation particle) is not translated (the FORMULAS regex anchors ^לך בדרך; the quotation
    mark does its work). Also: urḫu is written ITI ("month") there – a homophone spelling (arḫu / urḫu), noted.
  5. II.133 word order: יום יום – אֵתָנָה אל שַׁמַשׁ מתחנן: – the Akkadian has the name first (etana ūmišam-ma
    imtaḫḫara šamaš    ), but the ✓ formula requires ^יום יום, and the Hebrew keeps the two daily prayers (123, 133) visibly
    parallel.

II.136 ilī ukabbit eṭemmī aplaḫ את האלים כיבדתי, את האִטִּים יָרֵאתִי כִּי מְכַבְּדַי אֲכַבֵּד (שמואל א ב:ל); אַיֵּה כְבוֹדִי … אַיֵּה מוֹרָאִי (מלאכי א:ו) cognate kabātu D / כִּבֵּד; honour and fear as a pair.

II.137 šāʾilātu השואלות וְשֹׁאֵל אוֹב וְיִדְּעֹנִי וְדֹרֵשׁ אֶל הַמֵּתִים (דברים יח:יא) cognate šāʾilu / שֹׁאֵל: the Torah forbids the two acts of piety Etana lists (the "inquirers", the cult of the dead).
II.137 šāʾilātu, maššakkū השואלות, מֻגְמָרַי וַיִּשְׁאַל שָׁאוּל בַּיהוָה וְלֹא עָנָהוּ יְהוָה גַּם בַּחֲלֹמוֹת (שמואל א כח:ו) equivalent A king who tried every channel, dreams included, without answer – and then a woman diviner (28:7).
II.138 aslīya ina ṭubbuḫi ilū igdamrū את אֵילַי – בטבח – האלים גָּמְרוּ שָׂבַעְתִּי עֹלוֹת אֵילִים (ישעיהו א:יא) divergence Isaiah's God is "sated" with rams and refuses them; Etana's gods "finished" his rams and gave nothing. ṭabāḫu / טבח [cognate].
II.139 bēlī ina pîka liṣâm-ma אדוני – מפיך יֵצֵא מִלְּפָנֶיךָ מִשְׁפָּטִי יֵצֵא (תהלים יז:ב) equivalent The verdict "going out" from the god.
II.140 idnam-ma šamma ša alādi תנה לי את עשב הלידה תְּנִי נָא לִי מִדּוּדָאֵי בְּנֵךְ (בראשית ל:יד) divergence A fertility plant asked with "give me": mandrakes (דּוּדָאִים reserved) vs a plant in heaven. Also III.12.
II.140 idnam-ma תנה לי הָבָה לִּי בָנִים וְאִם אַיִן מֵתָה אָנֹכִי (בראשית ל:א) equivalent "Give me (sons)" – life and death.
II.142 piltī usuḫ נסח את חרפתי אָסַף אֱלֹהִים אֶת חֶרְפָּתִי (בראשית ל:כג) equivalent pištu / חֶרְפָּה (gated). Also MA d+4, III.14.
II.142 šuma šuknanni שִׂים לי שֵׁם כִּי אָמַר אֵין לִי בֵן בַּעֲבוּר הַזְכִּיר שְׁמִי (שמואל ב יח:יח); וְלֹא יִמָּחֶה שְׁמוֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל (דברים כה:ו) equivalent šumu = name and offspring; Absalom, without a son, sets up a pillar so that his name be remembered.
II.142 šuma šuknanni שִׂים לי שֵׁם וְנַעֲשֶׂה לָּנוּ שֵׁם (בראשית יא:ד) divergence A name made by building (Gen 11) vs a name asked of the god as a son.
II.146 ina libbīša nadi erû בלבה מושלך נשר אַךְ אֶל שְׁאוֹל תּוּרָד אֶל יַרְכְּתֵי בוֹר (ישעיהו יד:טו); וְאַתָּה הָשְׁלַכְתָּ מִקִּבְרְךָ (ישעיהו יד:יט) equivalent Isaiah 14 complete: "I will go up to heaven … and sit" (II.43, ET2) – brought down to the pit, "cast out". Also II.151, MA d+10.
II.152 ullânum-ma uštaqqâššu מיד – מגביה אותו מְקִימִי מֵעָפָר דָּל (תהלים קיג:ז) equivalent Raising from the depth.
OBM.b+10 išpil שָׁפַל גַּאֲוַת אָדָם תַּשְׁפִּילֶנּוּ (משלי כט:כג) equivalent The proud eagle brought low (also Obad 1:4, quoted in the entry).
OBM.b+12 šamšum qātī ṣabat שַׁמַשׁ, את ידי תפוס אָחַזְתָּ בְּיַד-יְמִינִי (תהלים עג:כג) equivalent The god who holds the hand; answered by II.132 and fulfilled in OBM c+1.
OBM.b+15 lemnēti kabtāti רעות כבדות וְחַטָּאתָם כִּי כָבְדָה מְאֹד (בראשית יח:כ) cognate "Heavy" sins (kabtu / כָּבֵד, gated).
OBM.c+1 qāssu iṣbatam את ידו תפס וְהַחֲזִיקִי אֶת יָדֵךְ בּוֹ (בראשית כא:יח) equivalent The promise of II.132 fulfilled, in the OB version.
OBM.c+2 ušētiqam šuttassu הֶעֱבִיר (אותו) את שוחתו וַיַּעֲלוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף מִן הַבּוֹר (בראשית לז:כח); וַיַּעֲלוּ אֹתוֹ מִן הַבּוֹר (ירמיהו לח:יג) equivalent Drawn up from the pit by men.
OBM.c+3 kīma nēšim nāʾerim כאריה שואג הַכְּפִירִים שֹׁאֲגִים לַטָּרֶף; וּלְבַקֵּשׁ מֵאֵל אָכְלָם (תהלים קד:כא) equivalent The roaring lion and its "food" (ukultu / אֹכֶל [cognate]).
OBM.c+4 emūqam īšu כוח – היה לו וְקוֹיֵ יְהוָה יַחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ יַעֲלוּ אֵבֶר כַּנְּשָׁרִים (ישעיהו מ:לא); תִּתְחַדֵּשׁ כַּנֶּשֶׁר נְעוּרָיְכִי (תהלים קג:ה) equivalent The eagle that renews its strength – the biblical image is the story's event.
OBM.c+6 ibrī lū itbārānū ana u attā רֵעִי, נהיה ידידים – אני ואתה וְעַתָּה לְכָה נִכְרְתָה בְרִית אֲנִי וָאָתָּה (בראשית לא:מד) equivalent The eagle offers Etana the very formula of the friendship he broke with the serpent (II.9, ET2).
OBM.c+7 qibiam-ma ša terrišanni luddikkum אמור לי – את אשר תשאל ממני – אֶתְּנָה לְךָ וְאֶתְּנָה כַּאֲשֶׁר תֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָי (בראשית לד:יב); שְׁאַל מָה אֶתֶּן לָךְ (מלכים א ג:ה) equivalent The open offer of a gift (Solomon's – in a night dream; cf. MA d+5–d+6).
OBM.c+9 īnīyā-mi pite katimtī את עיניי? פְּתַח – את נִסְתָּרִי גַּל-עֵינַי וְאַבִּיטָה נִפְלָאוֹת מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ (תהלים קיט:יח) equivalent Asking that the eyes be opened to the hidden. katimtu = נִסְתָּר (Gilgameš I 7, katimta ipte).
OBM.c+9 pite פְּתַח וְנִפְקְחוּ עֵינֵיכֶם; וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים (בראשית ג:ה); וַיִּפְקַח אֱלֹהִים אֶת עֵינֶיהָ (בראשית כא:יט) divergence petû = פָּתַח [cognate]; פָּקַח stays reserved. A man asks an eagle (MA d+3: the sun-god) to open his eyes.
MA.d+3 [īn]īya pite katmāti [את עי]ניי פְּתַח – (את) המכוסות וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מֵחַמָּתוֹ (תהלים יט:ז) equivalent Our proposal: nothing is hidden from the sun – the prayer to the sun-god to open the hidden.
MA.d+5–6 ittīl-ma etana ibarri … šutta īmur שָׁכַב אֵתָנָה, ובוחן … חלום ראה וַיִּשְׁכַּב בַּמָּקוֹם הַהוּא (בראשית כח:יא); בַּחֲלוֹם חֶזְיוֹן לַיְלָה … בִּתְנוּמוֹת עֲלֵי מִשְׁכָּב (איוב לג:טו); בַּחֲלוֹם הַלָּיְלָה (מלכים א ג:ה) equivalent Lying down to receive a dream (incubation); MA gives Šamaš's answer in a dream, SB in direct speech.
MA.e+8 attā-ma etana šar būli אתה הוא אֵתָנָה, מלך הבהמה וְגַם בַּהֲמוֹת שָׂדָי (תהלים ח:ח) equivalent The ruler of the animals; Foster's "wild beasts" narrows būlu.
MA.e+10 ištu qereb šuttati šūlânni מקרב השוחה – הַעֲלֵנִי וַיַּעֲלֵנִי מִבּוֹר שָׁאוֹן (תהלים מ:ג); וַתַּעַל מִשַּׁחַת חַיַּי (יונה ב:ז) cognate elû Š / הֶעֱלָה.
MA.e+13 ana ūm dārâti tanattaka [ל]יום נצחים – תהילתך לְדֹר וָדֹר נְסַפֵּר תְּהִלָּתֶךָ (תהלים עט:יג) equivalent The vow of praise – here vowed to a man (SB II.127: to Šamaš).
MA.e+16 ušellīka [אַעַלְךָ] וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה (בראשית מו:ד) cognate The same form, in God's promise to Jacob.
MA.f+2 ištu ṣīt šamši adi šalām šamši ממוצא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ – עד שקיעת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ מִמִּזְרַח-שֶׁמֶשׁ עַד-מְבוֹאוֹ (תהלים קיג:ג); מוֹשִׁיבִי עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת אֵם-הַבָּנִים שְׂמֵחָה (תהלים קיג:ט) equivalent Our proposal: Ps 113 joins "from sunrise to sunset", raising the poor from the dust (113:7) and the barren mother – the three motifs of MA e–f.
MA.f+5 anāku anaddinakku ša alādi šamma אני – אתן לך את עשב הלידה וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן (בראשית ב:ט) absent Foster's "plant of life" is a slip: the tablet has ša alādi "of birth" – no tree or plant of life in Etana (a false echo avoided).
MA.f+7 pūt būrti umdellâ את פְּאַת הבור – מילא וְהַבּוֹר רֵק אֵין בּוֹ מָיִם (בראשית לז:כד); וַיְשַׁלְּחֵם אֶל יִרְמְיָהוּ אֶל הַבּוֹר בַּחֲבָלִים (ירמיהו לח:יא) cognate būrtu / בּוֹר (gated), MA's only "cistern" (elsewhere šuttatu); a practical rescue from a pit, like Ebed-melech's rags and ropes.
MA.f+11 iṣabbuba agappīšu מנפנף באגפיו כְּנֶשֶׁר יָעִיר קִנּוֹ עַל גּוֹזָלָיו יְרַחֵף (דברים לב:יא) equivalent ṣabābu "flutter, flap" (Š: "teach fledglings to spread wings"); רִחֵף kept for the apparatus.
MA.f+14 u rebūti ו(פעם) רביעית וַיֹּאמֶר שֻׁב שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים (מלכים א יח:מג) equivalent Our proposal: an attempt repeated with a rising count until it succeeds.

Key findings

The Bible.

  1. Genesis 37 in a fable. The eagle's fate follows Joseph's step by step: "come, let us go down" (II.97 – לְכוּ,
    Gen 37:20), stripped – plucked (II.86, 120 ↔ 37:23), "thrown into the pit" with the same verb (nadû = הִשְׁלִיךְ;
    37:22, 24), a pit "without water" where he should die of hunger and thirst (II.87 ↔ 37:24), an anonymous "man" (II.132
    ↔ 37:15), and drawn up out of the pit (OBM c+2, MA e+10, f+7 ↔ 37:28). And Ps 105:17 says it in the god's voice:
    שָׁלַח לִפְנֵיהֶם אִישׁ (תהלים קה:יז) – exactly Šamaš's amēlu ša ašapparakku (II.132); Gen 45:5 כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹהִים לִפְנֵיכֶם (בראשית מה:ה).
  2. Isaiah 14 completed. ET2 found Isa 14:13 in the eagle's plan ("I will go up and dwell in heaven", II.43); ET3's lines
    complete it: the one who said it is "brought down to the depths of the pit" and "cast out" (Isa 14:15, 19) – the
    eagle "cast" in the pit (II.146, 151), "brought low" (OBM b+10 išpil; Prov 29:23, Obad 1:4).
  3. The lament psalms of the pit. The eagle's prayer (II.123–127) has their structure and vocabulary: prayer from the
    pit (Ps 88:5, 7; Lam 3:55), "keep me alive" (Ps 30:4, 119:25), and the vow of praise: "for days of eternity I will make
    your zikru heard" (II.127) – zikru / זֵכֶר [cognate], the same argument as Ps 6:6 and Ps 142:8. MA gives the vow
    to the man instead (e+13).
  4. The barren king's prayer and the "name". Etana's plea (II.140–142, MA d+4) meets Gen 30 (30:1, 14, 22–23), Isaac's
    and Hannah's repeated prayers (Gen 25:21, 1 Sam 1:7), and above all the "name" that only a son preserves (2 Sam 18:18,
    Deut 25:6, Ruth 4:10); Gen 11:4's name made by building is a [divergence].
  5. The piety the Torah forbids. Etana's claim on the god lists honouring the gods, revering the ghosts and the
    incense of the šāʾilātu (female inquirers) – Deut 18:11 forbids the שֹׁאֵל (šāʾilu [cognate]) and the inquirer of
    the dead, and Deut 26:14 boasts of giving nothing to the dead; 1 Sam 28:6–7 shows a king who did try dreams and a woman
    diviner. His argument "you ate, Šamaš … earth, you drank the blood" is what Ps 50:13 rejects; Isa 1:11 (rams) likewise.
  6. The bargain in the language of marriage. The eagle offers the serpent a bridegroom's nudunnû (II.114) – Gen
    34:12 מֹהַר וּמַתָּן וְאֶתְּנָה – and in OB offers Etana "tell me what you ask, I will give it" (OBM c+7), the same
    cohortative; 1 Kgs 3:5 ("ask what I shall give you", in a night dream) is the closest royal parallel.
  7. The serpent's refusal and 1 Kings 20. "If I release you, how shall I answer Šamaš? Your punishment would turn on me"
    (II.116–118) is the logic of 1 Kgs 20:42: the one who "released" (שִׁלַּחְתָּ = wuššuru) the man under the god's
    ban dies in his place.
  8. Small words and false echoes. kutum libbi is the caul fat of Lev 3:3 (the god's portion; II.83); petû =
    פָּתַח, not Gen 3:5's פָּקַח (OBM c+9, MA d+3); Foster's "plant of life" (MA f+5: the tablet has "of birth"),
    "lament" (II.73: unnīnu "supplication"), "Netherworld" (II.135), "no doubt" (II.100), "king of the wild beasts"
    (būlu), "tail feathers" (nuballu), "ambush" (šubtu "dwelling") – each checked against the Akkadian.

The ancient mind.

  1. Šamaš's justice and mercy, separated. He hears the wronged serpent, prepares the trap himself ("I have bound a wild
    ox for you"), makes the serpent his executioner; he will not save the oath-breaker ("you are under oath – I will not
    visit you") – yet he does not let him die: he "sends a man". He answers two prayers with one answer: a king without a
    son and an eagle without wings need each other.
  2. The serpent is an official, not an avenger. He refuses mercy for fear of answering to the god "above": the
    punishment he inflicts would fall on him if he relented – the logic of a deputy under oath.
  3. The pious king who has done everything. Fat sheep, the blood of rams poured on the earth, the gods honoured, the
    ghosts feared, the incense of the dream-women used up – and no son. Piety as a contract with the god, and the son as
    the one who will keep the father's "name" and feed his ghost: without him the king dies twice.
  4. Dreams as a technique. MA: Etana "lay down and examines (barû)" – incubation; the god answers in "the bed of the
    night"; SB has the same answer in direct speech; and the šāʾilātu used incense to obtain dreams.
  5. The hunter's world. A carcass as bait, a pitfall (šuttatu), birds of prey coming down in a crowd, the eagle that
    circles and pecks "in front and behind" before going in – exact observation of animals; and the recovery is slow:
    seven months, the eighth (OBM), attempt after attempt (MA f).
  6. Friendship as a renewable treaty. The eagle repeats to Etana the words with which he once bound himself to the
    serpent (OBM c+6 = II.9) – the second friendship rises out of the pit of the first; MA seals it "for ever" (e+17).
  7. A Hebrew-only pun: the cohortative "I will give" (אֶתְּנָה, II.114, OBM c+7) is spelt like Etana's name in
    Hebrew; kept vocalized, noted, not exploited.

Open decisions (numbered; the minor ones decided)

  1. kutum libbi = מִכְסֵה הַלֵּב instead of §10.3's מכסה הקרביים (decided; deviation 1).
  2. maṣû Št = חָדַר (II.83, 110; decided): ET2 restored MA c+22 uštamṣi? as הגיע?; הִגִּיעַ is kašādu
    (Gilgameš; II.90). Proposal for the coordinator: MA c+22 → אל מעי ה[ראם – חדר?].
  3. nuballu = מְנִיפוֹת (II.85, 119; decided, italic): Hebrew has no fourth wing word (כָּנָף kappu, אֵבֶר
    abru, נוֹצָה nāṣu, אֲגַף gappu/agappu; גַּף is gappu's cognate; זָנָב zibbatu); eBL "(eagle's) wing;
    also a form of snare?" – the spread wing or tail "like a fan". The coordinator may prefer a transliteration.
  4. šērtu = עֹנֶשׁ (II.117, 118, 125; OBM b+5; Atraḫasīs) vs אַשְׁמָה in Gilgameš I 238 and Ludlul III 58 – a
    cross-corpus split (lead). Here only "punishment" fits all four lines (אשמתך in II.125 would blame Šamaš).
  5. ērišu = חָתָן (II.114) collides with Gilgameš VI 42, 46, where ḫāmiru "husband, lover" is חתן (lead).
  6. sanāqu = בִּקֵּר (II.131; decided): "check" (Lev 13:36) and "come to (see)"; קָרַב qerēbu, נִגַּשׁ ṭeḫû,
    בָּא erēbu are taken.
  7. šubtu = מִשְׁכָּן (decided; deviation 3).
  8. sādu = מִגְרָשׁ (II.82, 110; decided): אָחוּ already carries Sum. u₂-sal (EA, Agade, Gudea, EWO) and Enūma
    eliš gipāru – a split the lead may want to look at.
  9. šuʾu = שֶׂה [cognate] (שֵׂיִי, collective; decided): צֹאן is ṣēnu (Enūma eliš VII 131).
  10. kubru = עֹבִי (decided; deviation 2).
  11. II.133 word order forced by the FORMULAS regex ^יום יום (deviation 5); the coordinator may relax the regex if
    אֵתָנָה – יום יום אל שַׁמַשׁ מתחנן: is preferred.
  12. unnīnu תַּחֲנוּנִים (harmonization) and maḫāru Gtn מִתְחַנֵּן (§10.3) share a Hebrew root – two pre-set
    renderings; kept (noun / verb), noted in II.73 (lead).
  13. etēqu Š = הֶעֱבִיר (OBM c+2; decided): הֶחֱלִיף means "exchange" (and is riābu in the law corpus); ebēru
    (whose Š would be העביר) does not occur in Etana – a note for later corpora.
  14. renderings §10.3, MA d+7 row: the tablet has etiq šadâm-ma (חלוף), not šadâ ebir – the row should be
    corrected (coordinator).
  15. ET1's OBM header paragraph quotes c+9 as "פקח את עיניי"; פָּקַח is reserved and the line has פְּתַח. I did
    not edit ET1's paragraph; my paragraph notes it (coordinator may correct).
  16. OBM b+9: eBL does not lemmatize er[îm, so the נשר gate has no licence there; the Hebrew הנ[שר (brackets per
    the ATF e-r[i-im) passes. If the tool should license by the normalization too, add erîm/erû to the ET gate.
  17. šaṭāṭu = שִׁסַּע (II.77, 91) beside Ur-Namma's Sum. šu sur₅ שסעו (italic) – minor.
  18. nāʾeru = שׁוֹאֵג (OBM c+3, MA f+16; Gilgameš V 124, 308) vs Atraḫasīs כנשר צורח – an existing split (lead).
  19. II.94 (statement or question) and II.124 (exclamation; Foster: question) – decided; alternatives in the notes.
  20. II.152 – subject of uštaqqâššu uncertain (Etana lifting the eagle, or the reverse); מגביה אותו keeps it open.
  21. mā = הֵן (OBM b+4); the restored [mā?] of MA d+7 is untranslated (formula anchor). Decided.

    לְאוֹת, סִיכָה, מוּפָעִים, כְּמוֹ מָה הִיא, כִּמְלֹא, מַרְבֵּץ, שֹׁקֶת, גַּנָּ[ן]; the punctuation of
    the repeated lines unified (all commands !, all executions .).

Deviations from renderings §10 and the briefs (decided at the first occurrence, with the reason)

  1. The flight's question is not ibrī amur māta mīnâ ibašši (renderings §10.3 and the brief quote the literature):
    the tablet has ibrī naplis-(ma) mātu kī mīni ibašši in the first flight (31, 35, 39) and dugul ibrī mātu kī
    ibašši     in the second (b+27, b+33, b+37; MA i+6, i+13) – two verbs, two word orders, mīni only in the first. So two
    strings: רֵעִי, הִסְתַּכֵּל – הארץ, כְּמוֹ מָה הִיא! (palāsu N = הִסְתַּכֵּל, ET2) and צְפֵה, רֵעִי – הארץ, איך היא! (dagālu = צָפָה, Gilgameš IX 174, Adapa, Theodicy). §10.3's row should be corrected.
  2. bēru + three verbs: ištēn / šanâ / šalša bēra + ullû (elû D) in the first flight and MA = העלה אותו
    (the root of elû kept, as Š הֶעֱלָה, MA e+10); šušqû (šaqû D) in the second = הגביה אותו (§10.3);
    nasāku in the drops = זרק אותו (Gilgameš XI 293 issukaššu זרקו; הִשְׁלִיךְ is nadû's).
  3. târu ana "turn into" = נֶהְפַּךְ לְ־ (Gilgameš XI 119, IV 106; Ludlul I 18, 84), not שָׁב (licensed by
    târu, but in Hebrew "return").
  4. kappu of Etana = כָּנָף (III.27, b+19), literal, against Foster's "hands": כַּף is rittu (Gilgameš VII 170,
    Ludlul V 12); the one Akkadian word for the eagle's wings and the man's "hands" is kept and footnoted.
  5. ina lēt = אֵצֶל (III.25), not צַד (Gilgameš IX 6 ana lēt אל צד), because §10.3 gives צַד to idu
    (III.26, b+28); lētu as a noun stays לְחִי.
  6. ṣīt šamši / ereb šamši: the coordinator's מִזְרַח שֶׁמֶשׁ / מְבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ were not used – neither phrase
    is in my lines (only ṣītu "outlet", III.16, a+8 = מוֹצָא, as ET3's MA f+2–f+3 מוֹצָא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ), and מָבוֹא is
    nērebu (ET2).
  7. palgu = תְּעָלָה (§10.3; = Sum. pa₅, Enki and the World Order 324) kept, although Enūma eliš VII 63 has the
    cognate פֶּלֶג (open decision 1); the cognate is tagged in MA i+10.
  8. mūšaru = עֲרוּגָה, kirû גַּן: kirû does not occur in my lines (the "garden" of Foster's MA i+9 is
    mūšaru), so גַּן was not used at all; nukaribbu = גַּנָּן (b+38).
  9. III.32's restored half-line is not translated (מְפַכִּ[ים? …]): eBL's nārātu? kī? palgî? is Foster's oral
    suggestion with three question marks, and Haul restores something else entirely.

Key findings

The Bible.

  1. Deuteronomy 32:11 and Exodus 19:4 told as a story. What the Bible uses as an image of God – the eagle that
    spreads its wings, takes up, carries on its pinion – is here a narrative in three movements: the eagle tells the man
    how to hold on (III.26–29; b+18–b+23), lifts him league after league, and, when he falls, dives and catches him on
    its wings four times (III.44–51 הנשר נפל – וקיבל אותו בכנפיו). The verb is the very cognate: luššīka
    "let me carry you" (b+17) = וָאֶשָּׂא אֶתְכֶם עַל כַּנְפֵי נְשָׁרִים (Exod 19:4) – but there God carries his people to
    himself, here an eagle carries a man to the gods.
  2. Isaiah 14 and Obadiah reversed. ET2 and ET3 found Isa 14:13–15 in the eagle's boast and fall (II.43, II.146);
    now the eagle lifts (šaqû D = הִגְבִּיהַּ, b+25; cf. Obad 1:4, Jer 49:16, Job 39:27) and the man says, with the
    same verb as the boast, "I will not go up to heaven" (III.42 ↔ II.43). The ascent in Etana is no hubris: Šamaš sends
    it, Ištar is its goal, a son its purpose. Against Gen 11:4 (וְרֹאשׁוֹ בַשָּׁמַיִם … וְנַעֲשֶׂה לָּנוּ שֵׁם) this is the
    clearest [divergence] of the corpus: a "name" (šumu) asked of the gods, not made against them.
  3. Genesis 28 and 37–41 in two versions of one dream. SB: Etana dreams that he and the eagle pass through the gates
    of Anu, Enlil, Ea, then of Sîn, Šamaš, Adad and Ištar, bowing at each, open a sealed house and see Ištar enthroned
    with lions; he wakes in terror (Gen 28:12–17 שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם, וַיִּיקַץ … וַיִּירָא); the friend says the dreams are
    plain; and the dream is fulfilled in its own words (b+40–b+45; Gen 41:13). The dreamer bows to the sun, moon and
    Venus gods – the exact reverse of Joseph's second dream (Gen 37:9). MA: two dreams instead, of kingship and plenty –
    plants gathered, heaps of loads in all the land, enemies "evil serpents" bowing beneath the dreamer – interpreted
    as "good" and "at your feet" (h+2–h+22): Joseph's sheaves (37:7), the doubled dream (37:9, 41:32), Joseph's heaps
    (41:49), the royal psalms (Ps 72:9, 110:1). The two versions show the same plot carrying two dream types: an
    ascent-vision and a kingship-dream.
  4. Throne visions. Ištar on a throne with lions under it (b+11–b+12) meets 1 Kgs 10:19–20 (the lion throne) and
    Isa 6:1 / Ezek 1:26 (the throne seen in heaven); the dreamer's prostration, Ezek 1:28.
  5. The earth from above (III.31–41, b+27–b+38): Isa 40:22 וְיֹשְׁבֶיהָ כַּחֲגָבִים; the vocabulary of the view is
    agricultural – מַרְבֵּץ (tarbaṣu [cognate], Ezek 25:5, Zeph 2:15), עֲרוּגָה (mūšaru), שֹׁקֶת, תְּעָלָה, a
    gardener's dike. (Our proposal:) Ezekiel's eagle parable, which ET2 found in the poplar and the oath, also has the
    garden "beds" (עֲרֻגוֹת, Ezek 17:7, 10) and the wing words כָּנָף / אֵבֶר / נוֹצָה (17:3) = kappu / abru /
    nāṣu: Ezek 17 is the closest biblical counterpart of the whole Etana imagery.
  6. Hannah and Leah. If NinNA1 belongs to Tablet III, Etana "reached his city and his house" and a woman speaks to
    him about the plant of birth, a salve(?), cooking (a+4–a+9): the return home after the prayer (1 Sam 1:19) and the
    plant passed between wife and husband (Gen 30:14–16; דּוּדָאִים reserved).
  7. False echoes avoided: Foster's "sacred bond" (ellu "pure", MA h+2), "made understand" (maḫāru Š),
    "hands" (kappu "wings"), "wearing a tiara" (ruṣṣunat, of a powerful voice), "garden" (mūšaru "bed"), "brook /
    watery" (the obscure mēmē), "rivers … like brooks" (a restoration); סֻלָּם, רָקִיעַ, פָּתַר, מִגְדָּל kept out
    of the Hebrew lines; pašāru = פָּשַׁר.

The ancient mind.

  1. The eagle as a royal vehicle. Akkad-period cylinder seals (24th–22nd centuries BCE) show a man carried up on an
    eagle's back while shepherds and dogs look up: the story is a millennium and a half older than the Nineveh tablets.
  2. The world seen by an irrigation farmer. From above, the land becomes a garden bed, the sea a sheepfold, a
    trough, the water of a canal, a gardener's dike; the rivers trickle. The ancient imagination measured height in
    double-hours of walking (bēru) and the last drop in half-reeds (III.50).
  3. Fear and failure without blame. At the third league the king who wanted heaven cannot see the land and asks to
    be put down on a path and walk to his city; the eagle does not argue, but lowers him in four drops, catching him
    each time. The first flight fails; the second, after a dream, succeeds.
  4. Dreams as the gods' language, read by a friend. Not a professional interpreter but the eagle says "your dreams
    are plain" (SB) or "your dream is good" (MA); the "good dream" is a category of Babylonian dream lore; the dreamer
    wakes trembling (as Gudea did); the dream is fulfilled to the letter.
  5. The court of heaven. The gates follow the gods' rank: the great triad (Anu, Enlil, Ea), then the astral gods
    (Sîn, Šamaš, Ištar) and Adad; at each gate one bows, as at a king's audience; at the end, a sealed storehouse
    (sealings with cylinder seals), a door pushed open, and the goddess enthroned with her lions.
  6. Ištar, giver of birth and of kingship. The plant is "with Ištar the lady" (III.24): the goddess who sought a
    shepherd for Kiš (I.19–22) holds the means of an heir; the gardener of b+38 belongs to her world (Išullānu,
    Sargon).
  7. Understanding the birds. SB adds what the older versions take for granted: man and eagle need Šamaš's gift to
    understand each other (III.3–8) – the speech of birds as a divine favour.
  8. The kingship-dream in MA: the "pure bond above" (markasu, the cosmic bond of heaven and earth, cf. Dur-an-ki),
    tribute heaped up, the enemies as "evil serpents" bowing – the fable's serpent turned into the vanquished foe of a
    king.
  9. The lost end. The Sumerian King List names Etana's son Balīḫ as his successor; Gilgameš VII sees Etana among the
    dead: tradition knew both the son and the death.

Open decisions (numbered; the minor ones decided)

  1. palgu = תְּעָלָה (renderings §10.3; Enki and the World Order's pa₅) vs פֶּלֶג [cognate] (Enūma eliš
    VII 63; Ps 1:3 פַּלְגֵי מָיִם): the Hebrew cognate is hidden here (guidelines §6.4: among equally good renderings
    prefer the cognate). Proposal for the lead: palgu = פֶּלֶג everywhere (MA i+10 would read [כ]מי פלג), Sum. pa₅
    following it. Settled 2026-10-23 (../../harmonization--2026-10-23.md row 7): palgu = פֶּלֶג; Sum. pa₅ keeps תְּעָלָה.
  2. buginnu = שֹׁקֶת (= Sum. buniĝ, Gudea B xvii 8 שוקתות) collides with Gilgameš I's mašqû שוקת. Proposal:
    mašqû "watering place" = מַשְׁקֶה [cognate] in Gilgameš, שֹׁקֶת left to buginnu / buniĝ (lead).
  3. galātu = הִתְפַּלֵּץ (III b+14), parādu = נִבְהַל (Ludlul I 54); but Gudea's Sumerian ḫuluḫ (= galātu)
    is נבהל (A xii 13). The Sumerian rule ("a Sumerian word takes the Hebrew of its Akkadian equivalent") would give
    ḫuluḫ התפלץ; minor (lead).
  4. qarānu / qurunnu = עָרַם / עֲרֵמָה (MA h+16) beside EA's Sum. dub ערם (= Akk. šapāku / tabāku,
    Gilgameš XI tabāku צבר): an older split; minor.
  5. īku = סוֹלְלָה (b+38; Enūma eliš, EWO eg₂): kept for consistency, although the image here is the ditch; the
    note explains. Decided.
  6. kappu of Etana = כָּנָף (literal; footnote), not כַּף (rittu). Decided (deviation 4).
  7. maḫāru Š (šutta ušamḫir) = הִקְבִּיל (italic; G קִבֵּל), Foster's "made understand" in the apparatus;
    the subject "the eagle" is eBL's restoration. Decided.
  8. mēmē(-ma) = מים (a+19, b+30, b+34, MA i+3; italic): eBL rejects NABU 2012/21's mê palgi. Decided.
  9. ṣâdu = צָד [cognate] (III.21; ET2 reserved צָד for it), vocalized against צַד (idu). Decided.
  10. NinNA1 (a+1–a+23) follows eBL's placement in Tablet III; the notes say "if it belongs here". Decided.
  11. Speech boundaries in III.12–19 (Etana 12–17, the eagle 18–19 without a speech formula) follow Foster. Decided.
  12. tēqītu = סִיכָה (a+7; vocalized: EWO's סיכה "pin" is kirid); tarāku = הוֹלֵם (III.52; EA's
    הולם "befitting" is Sum. tum₂, another word): homographs, minor.
  13. III.32's restoration left untranslated (deviation 9). Decided.
  14. bēru בֵּרוּ vocalized at every occurrence (unvocalized "they chose"); the lead may add it to TRAPS.
  15. renderings §10.3, the flights row: ibrī amur māta mīnâ ibašši is not on the tablet (deviation 1); and
    §10.3's agappu / gappu, nāṣu, ṣīt/ereb šamši rows: only nāṣu and agappu occur in ET4 (coordinator).

Notes for the clean translation

For the coordinator's introduction to the whole epic (translation--intro.rtl.md):

  1. Six fragmentary versions, one story, no end. OB Morgan and Susa (18th–17th c. BCE), the MA tablets from Aššur
    (13th–11th c.), and SB I–III from Nineveh (7th c.); every version is broken, and the end of the epic is lost in all.
    Labels like a+1 mark the first preserved line after a gap of unknown length; [ ], …, ? and italics are part
    of the text, not decoration.
  2. The plot in four movements: kingship comes down from heaven and Kiš has a king but no heir (OBM, SB I); the
    fable of the eagle and the serpent – oath, betrayal, Šamaš's trap, the eagle in the pit (OBS, MA a–c, SB II); the
    childless king's prayer and the rescue of the eagle (SB II, OBM b–c, MA d–f); the dreams and the two flights to
    heaven (SB III, MA g–i). The fable is not a digression: the two needs – a king without a son, an eagle without
    wings – are joined by the god.
  3. Šamaš directs everything: judge of the oath, maker of the trap, sender of the "man", giver of the speech of
    birds. Ištar holds the plant of birth and sits enthroned with lions at the top of heaven.
  4. Key words kept as the Akkadian has them: שֵׁם (šumu) is both "name" and "offspring"; עשב הלידה is the "plant
    of birth" (Foster's "plant of life" in MA f+5 is an error); רֵעִי (ibrī) is the eagle's and Etana's word for each
    other; בֵּרוּ is a "double hour" of walking, c. 10 km (three of them c. 30 km); a half-reed (חֲצִי קָנֶה) c. 1.5 m.
  5. Repetition is the art. Identical Akkadian has identical Hebrew: the speech formulas, the oath and its curses,
    the hunt refrain, Šamaš's command and its execution, the plea, the leagues of the flights, the eagle's "look, my
    friend", the drops, and above all the dream and its fulfilment "in the same words" (III b+3–b+8 ↔ b+40–b+45).
    Where a copy differs by a word, the Hebrew differs by that word.
  6. The versions differ in meaningful ways: SB alone has the speech of birds and the dream of the gods' gates and
    of Ištar; MA alone has two kingship-dreams (Joseph-like), the eagle's identifying Etana and its vow, and gives the
    description of the shrinking earth to Etana; the OB tablets are the shortest and the most direct.
  7. Names are vocalized where unvocalized Hebrew would mislead: אֵתָנָה (not "אֶתְּנָה", "I will give"), שַׁמַשׁ
    (the god) vs הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ (the sun), אָנוּ (not "we"), סִין, אִשְׁתַּר, שַׁכַּן, אִט (a ghost).
  8. Biblical words deliberately absent from the Hebrew text (they belong to the notes): סֻלָּם, מִגְדָּל,
    רָקִיעַ, עֲקָרָה, דּוּדָאִים, גּוֹזָל, פָּקַח, פָּתַר, חֵרֶם, שְׁאוֹל; נֶשֶׁר, נָחָשׁ, שׁוּחָה, בּוֹר, רֶשֶׁת,
    פַּח, חֶרְפָּה, נוֹצָה, אֵבֶר appear only for their Akkadian counterparts.
  9. The afterlife of the story: Akkad-period seals (24th–22nd c.) show the man on the eagle; the Sumerian King List
    calls Etana "the shepherd who went up to heaven" and names his son Balīḫ as successor; in Gilgameš VII Etana sits in
    the house of dust (יושב אֵתָנָה, יושב שַׁכַּן).
  10. The main biblical comparisons (for the reader of the commentary): Gen 11:4 and Isa 14:12–15 (ascent and fall,
    as [divergence]); Exod 19:4 and Deut 32:11 (the carrying eagle); Gen 28:12–17 (the dream of heaven's gate);
    Gen 37 and 40–41 (dreams, doubled dreams, interpretation; the pit); Gen 30 and 1 Sam 1 (the plea for a child, the
    "name"); Ezek 17 (eagle, poplar, oath, net, garden beds); 1 Kgs 10:19–20 (the lion throne).
